long_biography.plain_text:
After qualifying in medicine in Perm, Dmitry Rybolovlev joined his scientist father in a medical-services venture before moving into securities trading. Russia's voucher privatisation provided the larger opening: he acquired stakes in regional companies, concentrated his investments in Uralkali and secured voting control. As chairman, he introduced new governance practices and took the potash producer public in London.

Rybolovlev sold his Uralkali interests in 2010 and redirected the proceeds into businesses spanning health, food and entertainment. He became majority shareholder and president of AS Monaco the following year, when the club was struggling in France's second division. Promotion, a 2017 league title, European campaigns and new training facilities followed. A substantial biotechnology fund, property and art holdings illustrate the broader investment portfolio that succeeded Uralkali, while football remains his most sustained public operating role.
